name: RAG Hallucination Benchmark for Teaching Knowledge Bases
description: How often does a small RAG system invent answers when the knowledge base does not contain them? This benchmark measures hallucination rates of a 0.5B model (Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct) on 30 teaching-domain questions (10 answerable / 10 partial / 10 unanswerable) across 3 RAG configurations. Key finding: 30-70% hallucination rate despite explicit grounding instructions; increasing top_k from 3 to 5 halved hallucinations. Part of Study Intelligence, the open research program of the Atlanta College of Liberal Arts and Sciences (ACLAS).
